text_fidelity_a:
CanaKit Raspberry Pi 3 Complete Starter Kit - 32 GB Edition This is a very complete kit and does contain everything you need to setup a Raspberry Pi 3. Yes, the op system installs easily and, with luck, you can be up and running in less than an hour. So, why the 2 stars?

It gets 2 stars because the Raspberry Pi is probably one of the most frustrating devices I've ever tried to put to any real use. For example, I wanted to set it up so I could use a VNC server on the Pi and a VNC client on my Mac (OS X El Capitan). After three days of almost non-stop failures, I'm sick of this thing. Researching how to get this task done leads you down a black hole of internet articles and posts on the Raspberry Pi site, most of that give different instructions, use different commands, tell you which files to edit and what to put in them, and almost none work, period!

The core problem rests squarely on the Raspberry Pi organization. Their own website is full of conflicting posts on how to do just about anything beyond a basic setup. Few, if any posts state which model of Pi is being referenced, and many bear no date. All in all, it's a very frustrating experience and, while I like to tinker with these things, a little success is required once in a while to keep me chugging along. I think I'm done with this thing. I had hoped it would finally be a Linux for the rest of us. Unfortunately, it's just as convoluted and difficult to use as any version of Linux out there (my opinion).

However, if you're looking to explore the Pi, this kit has everything you need to do a basic setup of Linux. And, should you want to use it as a web server, file server, media server, you're really on your own. Drink lots of coffee and plan to pull our lots of hair.
text_fidelity_b: CanaKit Raspberry Pi 3 Complete Starter Kit - 32 GB Edition

I would recommend this product to others who are looking to save a little bit of money

text_fidelity_a:
JVC Soft Wireless Earbud with Stayfit Tips, Remote and Mic and Bluetooth Violet (HA-FX9BTV) 3.5 stars taking price into account

With headphones, it is always a blend of "you get what you paid for", and comparing to others at a similar price point.
How do these compare? Well, they are about average for the $20-$40 range. Not much better, not much worse. And as is the case with headphones, for a bit more, you can do MUCH better, and for a bit less, you will get roughly similar results. (In other words, headphones under $75-$100 are, more or less very similar, and then suddenly, your options get drastically better.)

Here's my analysis on the general sound quality and other features:

MISC:
Phone calls: 5 stars: Easy to use, works great for calls on both ends, and blocks outside sound quite well!
Ease of use/pairing: 5 stars: It passed the test of not having to read instructions, meaning it is incredibly simple to pair and use
Appearance: 5 stars: Neat! It's colorful and fun, as well as practical and functional!
External noise: 4 stars: Because it has a pretty tight seal, it is like an earplug, blocking outside sound quite effectively
Comfort: 3 stars: comparable to others of this design. Totally fine at first, and annoying after long use.

SOUND:
Treble: 2 stars: quite tinny
Bass: 2 stars: ok depth, not great, not very powerful
Overall: 2 stars: not much detail in the sound, but it can get pretty loud without distorting, and it is definitely good enough for basic listening and phone calls. There also appears to be a *very slight* hiss in quiet/silent moments when the volume is louder.

OVERALL:
The average is 28 out of 40 possible points, or 70% (a "C" grade, if it were going to school ;-), but because the above analysis does not take price point into account, comparing this to brands like Bose, as well as dollar store headphones, this means that for the current list price of roughly $29.99, this is a reasonable expectation.

The average number of stars based on my rubric is 3.5 stars: decent for this price point, and certainly good enough to enjoy music and spoken word, and to have successful phone calls.
text_fidelity_b: JVC Soft Wireless Earbud with Stayfit Tips, Remote and Mic and Bluetooth Violet (HA-FX9BTV)

text_fidelity_a:
Perixx Periboard-512 Ergonomic Split Keyboard - Natural Ergonomic Design - Black - Bulky Size 19.09"x9.29"x1.73", US English Layout First let me tell you what I like about this keyboard: I like the key action. Keys have a decently long stroke and are easy to press and don't feel spongy. I like the split layout, which makes for a much more natural position for the arms. I like the split spacebar. To me, these are advantages over the Logitech K350 I've been using, which has a curved, not split, key layout and a spongy feel when typing.

What I don't like, and what was pretty much a dealbreaker to me (I thought about returning it almost immediately) is the "wrist rest." It is short and rolls off steeply and provides no wrist support at all, unless you like typing with your wrist positioned lower than your knuckles and your hands bent upwards from the wrist. The recommended position is wrist level with the knuckles, which is called the "neutral" position. I personally prefer typing with my wrists positioned slightly higher than my knuckles.

Look at the product photos and notice that the typist doesn't even have his wrist on the wrist rest. He or she is using a hover hand technique, I guess to make things look more ergonomic or something, because if their wrists were actually on the wrist rest, their hands would be obviously bent upwards at the wrists to reach the keys.

I'm at a loss as to why many keyboard manufacturers (including Logitech with the K350) provide legs to raise the back of the keyboard and don't provide anything to raise the front. That just makes the "backwards" bend at the wrist even more pronounced.

This Periboard keyboard is no exception to that. It has foldaway legs at the back and none in the front. But even if it had legs to raise the front, it wouldn't provide much improvement. I raised the front a couple of inches with a foam wedge I use for keyboard support, and the wrist rest was still so low I pressed the spacebar when reaching for the F2 key.

I even tried adding foam wrist rests but the built-in rest is so steep and short it actually interferes with using a really functional rest. I even tried using wearable wrist rests---which are kind of annoying on their own since they aren't all that stable---and the steep slope and short length of the built-in wrist rest made that a less than effective solution. This keyboard might have been a lot better if it had no built-in wrist rest at all. That way you could use your own and set it up just like you like it.

It's disappointing, actually. I like the key action and layout, but the wrist rest pretty much nerfs the whole thing. I may keep it and experiment with solutions from time to time. I might even see if I can cut off the built-in rest and replace it with something made of wood or something, or just get it out of the way so I can use some other effective wrist rest.

In the meantime, I'm probably going to stick with the spongy-action, non-split Logitech K350. In fact I'm typing this review on it, though I would have liked to use the Periboard 512. But until I come up with a better wrist rest solution it's just easier to use the K350.

And a couple more quick points, comparing this keyboard to the K350, this keyboard is wired while the K350 is wireless. The overall footprint of both (length and width) is almost the same. I personally don't use or need the multimedia keys on either.

Because of the better key action and, to me, better key layout, if it had a better wrist rest, or none at all, this Periboard 512 might have become my go-to keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: Perixx Periboard-512 Ergonomic Split Keyboard - Natural Ergonomic Design - Black - Bulky Size 19.09"x9.29"x1.73", US English Layout

I would purchase again. LOVE this camera. Would make a kid or an enthusiastic camera junkie a very nice present.
I received this camera for free for testing and reviewing purposes. This is my honest unbiased opinion and have come to it by using the camera myself.

text_fidelity_a: Fire HD 8 Tablet (8" HD Display, 16 GB) - Black (Previous Generation - 8th) This was such a wonderful surprise Christmas gift from my husband! I had wanted one since my Sony E-reader broke 7+ years ago! I have been using the kindle app on my phone for years but as my age progress my eyes regress. I went from no glasses to wearing 2.0 reading glasses in just under 2 years. I'm now able to read more and turn less pages. I'm in love with my new Kindle! If there are cons they are that 1) it's not pink! Why would anything ever be made in any color other than pink? Insanity! And 2) it doesn't come with a case. It's weighty and my hands tire of holding it as I'm reading myself to sleep at night. I'm still shopping for a cover that will sit stable on my stomach in bed while I read. And lastly 3) out charges with a micro USB not a new C-type. All of my devices had already upgraded to C-type so finding a long micro in the house was a pain. And after just 1 month the cable is back to the old ways of micro cables. Loosening, falling out, ba-ding ba-ding. Ugghh why hasn't it been changed to the new C-type???? The C-type cables don't do that mess. So yeah that's a negative. But overall I'm tickled pink with my table even if it isn't pink. 😇

Today my external hard drive is not recognized when it is plugged into this hub. I am NOT restarting my computer to test whether it is necessary to have the HDD recognized. It IS recognized when it is plugged into a different hub that is also plugged into my Mac mini.

Since my 4-bay HDD enclosure has to remain connected for the hourly Time Machine backups, it is now connected directly to my Mac mini. The only reason to keep this hub is for charging any device.

UPDATE (2/15/2019):
Other drives (SSD and HDD) that were connected to this hub also disconnected themselves. The wired Apple aluminum keyboard (it came with my 2008 Mac Pro) is plugged into this hub, and it does not generate the warning that the device was disconnected. If I were shopping for a USB hub, I would stay away from this one. Nothing is "deluxe" except the name - and the lighted ports.

UPDATE (2/9/2019):
My devices - SSDs and 4-bay HDD enclosure - that are plugged into this hub have been disconnecting for no apparent reason. I thought my Logitech mouse was disconnecting because the dongle was plugged into it, but that seems to be the fault of the dongle since it continued while plugged into my keyboard. I have moved my keyboard cable to the hub, and we will see how long that lasts. The 4-bay enclosure is more critical, so it is connected to a USB port on my computer. When the enclosure was connected to this hub, I kept seeing that warning that my drives were Not Ejected Properly

Connected this to my computer's USB 3.0 port. Plugged in the dongle for my battery powered mouse. Mouse began acting erratically, had to remove the dongle and reinsert it to reconnect. Functioned properly for a short while but disconnected.
Finally had to plug dongle in the port on my wired keyboard before it would stay connected and not perform erratically. Something must be interrupting the signal even when the LEDs indicate the hub is connected even during periods when my computer is asleep.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (1/25/2019):
The hub has 3 smart charging ports, but when viewed from an angle, only the two on the end have orange / red LED light showing - the 3rd one appears blue. All lights are bright - brighter than they need to be.

A 4-bay HDD enclosure is plugged into this hub and has been functioning without any problem for the 2 weeks I have had the enclosure connected. Connecting an SSD through this hub also functions with no problem using a SATA-USB3 cable.

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung BD-H5900 3D Blu-Ray Disc Player (2014 Model) Packaging--very minimal, which is nice. Box was just enough to fit the machine safely and snugly--no over packaging

Set up--lightning fast. Pop two (included) batteries in the remote, attach to TV, plug in, choose a language, connect to home wi-fi and ready to go in two minutes at the most. Check for software upgrade, there is one, download--all done in another minute.

Apps: Seems to be a lot of back and forth on Amazon Prime. Mine definitely does not support. These are the apps from the newest software update (June 20th, 2014)
hulu plus,
VUDU
Youube
Netflix
Opera TV store
Flixster
CinemaNow
Rhapsody
Picasa
AccuWEather
Twitter
Pandora
Target
Internet TV--horrible interface
Flickr
Facebook

To be honest, I wouldn't use most of these, so I'm not all that impressed with the Apps, though certainly they have the most needed on one in Netflix. But as I have Amazon Prime, I'm sticking with our DVD player that allows me to access it (I also have an Apple TV, which is why these apps don't do much for me). I'll also say some of these apps had terrible interfaces (yes, I'm looking at you Internet TV)

Build quality: I don't know if it really matters at all with a DVD player--I mean, it's going to sit up there and not really get any abuse I assume. But it does feel a bit light, not all that solid. If it were something portable and had that feel, I'd have some concerns. Not so much with this kind of device. It has a relatively small footprint.

I had not problem with several DVDs, both blu-ray and regular. Menu movement was fast, start-up time no different from any others I've used--not noticeably better or worse. Picture was fine, again, no better or worse than others I've sued (Sony, JVC)

screen is a bit too bright. Personally, I'd find it annoying, but others may not notice.

It's not a bad player at all, does most of what it needs to OK, but I definitely prefer our Sony for its larger app features and dimmer screen (it also feels more sturdy).
text_fidelity_b: Samsung BD-H5900 3D Blu-Ray Disc Player (2014 Model)
